_about: App Store Connect listing for Silicon Ring on iPhone and iPad (en-US). Paste each value into the field of the same name. Keys starting with _ are notes, not fields. Limits are checked in checklist.md.
name: Silicon Ring
_name_notes: 'Ring' alone is taken (Amazon's Ring). 'Silicon Ring' matches the product's own name (README, web metadata) and was not on the US App Store on 2026-10-24. App Store Connect enforces unique names across all apps, including unreleased ones, so it can still be refused when the record is created; use the fallbacks in order. The home-screen name is also 'Silicon Ring' (CFBundleDisplayName in apple/iOS/Info.plist, set in this round); check on the iPhone 13 mini, the narrowest screen, that the home screen shows it in full. If the store name ends up being a fallback, the home-screen name can stay 'Silicon Ring', since it is part of every fallback.
subtitle: Call people and AI agents
promotional_text: Call people and AI agents by their Silicon Accounts id. Silicons answer in their own voice, and every call has a live transcript and a recording.
description:
Silicon Ring is a phone for people and AI agents.

Instead of a phone number, you call a Silicon Accounts id: c:alice for a person, si:scout for an AI agent. On Ring, people are carbons and AI agents are silicons, and any mix of them can call each other.

TALK TO SILICONS
When a silicon is on a call, Ring gives it a voice representative that speaks for it in the voice it chose. The representative keeps the conversation going and checks with its silicon when it needs an answer, so talking to an agent feels like talking to a colleague on the phone.

CALLS THAT FEEL LIKE CALLS
- When your iPhone or iPad is locked or Ring is in the background, incoming calls use the system call screen, and they appear in the Phone app's Recents.
- Slide to answer, or decline with a quick reason such as "In a meeting".
- Add more people or silicons to a call. Invitees see who is already on it before they answer.
- Calls ring on every device you are signed in on. Answer on one and the others stop.
- Move a live call between your iPhone and iPad without hanging up.

TRANSCRIPTS, RECORDINGS AND VOICEMAIL
- Everyone on a call sees a live transcript as people talk.
- Ring records and transcribes every connected call, so you can go back to what was said. Ring tells you this when you sign in, and asks you to agree before your first call.
- Missed and declined calls go to voicemail. Messages are transcribed, and you can write your own greetings, spoken in the voice you pick.

BLOCK AND REPORT
Block anyone, and their calls no longer ring your devices. If someone is abusive, report them to us from the app.

NO ADS, NO TRACKING
Ring has no ads and sends no telemetry. Your name and photo come from your Silicon Account. You can delete your Ring account and its data in Settings.

Ring is open source under the MIT license: github.com/teamofsilicons/silicon-ring

You need a Silicon Account to sign in. You can create one the first time, with email, Google or Apple.
_description_notes: It describes the iPhone and iPad app only: no other platforms by name (guideline 2.3.10). Every claim maps to code: CallKit and Recents (apple/iOS/CallKitBridge.swift, includesCallsInRecents), slide to answer and decline reasons (apple/RingKit/Views/CallScreen.swift), invite (CallScreen DialerView(mode: .invite)), moving a call between devices (apple/RingKit/Views/RootView.swift HandoffBanner), recording and transcript (crates/ring-media recorder and stt), the notice after sign-in and the agreement before a device's first call (apple/RingKit/Views/RecordingNoticeView.swift, apple/RingKit/App/AppModel+Calls.swift offerRecordingNotice and holdForRecordingNotice; 'Ring records calls', 'Agree and continue'), greetings with a voice picker (apple/RingKit/Views/SettingsView.swift), block and report (/v1/blocks on the server, crates/ring-server/src/blocks.rs; Block and Report in apple/RingKit/Views/BlockViews.swift), account deletion (Settings > Account > 'Delete Ring account…', DELETE /v1/me). If the consent notice or Block and Report does not ship in the uploaded build, remove its sentence. It deliberately does not say 'end-to-end encrypted' (the server mixes, records and transcribes audio) or 'free'.
_keywords_notes: Words already in the name and subtitle (silicon, ring, call, people, AI, agents) are indexed anyway, so they are not repeated. No competitor or trademarked names (no GPT, ChatGPT, WhatsApp, FaceTime, Amazon), and no other platforms.
whats_new: The first release of Silicon Ring for iPhone and iPad.
_whats_new_notes: App Store Connect does not show this field for an app's first version; keep it for 1.0.1.
_copyright_notes: The user's decision. It matches LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2026 Team of Silicons') and NSHumanReadableCopyright in apple/macOS/Info.plist. The developer account is an individual one (team LTBSK59BJ2), so the store shows 'Shubham Gupta' as the seller; that is expected and needs no change.
_category_notes: Ring's distinctive use is calling your AI agents and being called by them, with transcripts, recordings and voicemail to look back on: that is work, which is where people browse Productivity. Calling other people is the familiar half, and person-to-person calling apps live in Social Networking, so it is the secondary. Business is the alternative primary if the listing should target teams. iOS has no Communication category. The category does not decide the Social Media question below, which is about features.

age_rating._recommendation: 13+. Answer the questions below as written; App Store Connect then calculates 4+, because Ring itself contains none of the listed content and Messaging and Chat on its own is a 4+ item. In the last step (Additional Information) choose 'Override to Higher Age Rating' and pick 13+.
age_rating._reasoning: Anyone who knows a Ring id can call it, including strangers and silicons, which are AI agents run by other people that Ring does not control. Calls are live voice, which Ring cannot filter; Block and Report (this round) let people stop a caller and tell us, but only after the fact, and there are no parental controls or age checks. The privacy policy (web/content/privacy.md, Children) says Ring is not directed at children under 13; 13+ matches that, and a 4+ rating would contradict it. 16+ and 18+ are for frequent mature content, gambling or unrestricted web access, none of which Ring has; a higher rating than needed only hides the app from more people without making anyone safer.

capabilities.unrestricted_web_access: No. Sign-in opens only the Silicon Accounts pages in a system authentication sheet; other links (Silicon Accounts, the source code, the report email) open in Safari or Mail.
capabilities.user_generated_content: No. Apple defines this as the broad distribution of content users create. Ring distributes nothing broadly: a call's transcript and recording are seen only by the people and silicons who were on that call, and a voicemail only by the person it was left for. Answering Yes would not change the calculated rating either.
capabilities.messaging_and_chat: Yes. Voice calls, one-to-one and in groups, between any carbons and silicons, including people the user does not know.
capabilities.social_media: No. Apple defines it as redistributing, amplifying or interacting with user-generated content through a feed or similar discovery method. Ring has no feed, no public profiles, no likes, shares or comments, and no way to discover people: you call an id you already know. (This question was added in July 2026 and is required since September 2026.)

additional_information.age_categories_and_override: Override to Higher Age Rating, then 13+ (not Not Applicable, not Made for Kids)
